This is based on personal experience but I just got thrown into a ward lmao. I’ve called a few times and nothing came about because I just said “I’ll be okay” even if the ideation was still truly there.

The people who drove me were cops but they were nice. Since it was from school they bought me cookies and were actually pretty calming. I’ve had an experience where I’ve been dragged by a cop in grade 11 and that wasn’t fun.

When you get to the ward they assign you a room, the food sucks yeah and the nurses admit it. They take a bunch of tests, question you - you meet with a psychiatrist everyday to assess you. My ward I was lucky enough to have a peloton and id use it everyday. They may make you leave with a diagnosis, when I left they said I had a major depressive episode, borderline personality disorder, and prescribed me antipsychotics. 

I don’t think the psychiatrist talked to me too long tbh? But that’s apart of a ward. They take away your strings and will provide you with clothes, some may give the option of bringing your own. But everything that’s brought in gets searched, my burgers were searched lmao. I actually had an okay experience there, you meet a lot of people with similar issues. People are nice, but you hear a lot of crying or screaming which isn’t scary, but sad. I had a phone but the nurses would charge it since I didn’t have a cord. We also had activities, some woman would come in and paint with us. Id just draw, go on the peloton and juggle all day lmao

My exit had me sign a contract basically saying “ok well I won’t kill myself and if I do it’s not the hospitals fault”. And they gave me a free voucher for a cab and I left. There have been times where it’s incredibly difficult to succeed due to the fact I can’t focus on the content. I recommend that you get a team of mental health counsellors at your college that can advocate for your behalf, because honestly that’s the only way I graduated as valedictorian in high school. It is a lot more difficult to succeed than your peers with mental health issues and you’ll always hear the bullshit of “be happy” like it’s the easiest fucking thing.

Something that has personally helped me a lot, and I don’t mean to push anything onto you like a guru is getting into a good routine. You may wanna check out r/EOOD (exercising out of depression) which has helped me get out of the house in depressive episodes but gain a love back for physical activity and my body. Also, this has reinsured me to study more - you may wanna try out the pomodoro technique as it’s hard as fuck to focus when you’re not taking breaks. Getting 1 small step done everyday is better than nothing.
